newsitem.title: INDIA: Rupee slips as India state bank resumes dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Rupee slips as India state bank resumes dlr buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed lower at 35.8900/8950 on Thursday after a state-run bank entered the market, ending weeks of inactivity, dealers said.
The rupee had opened Thursday at 35.86/87 per dollar. The state-run bank, the market's most influential player, had been inactive this month.
"The spell has been broken at last," a dealer said, referring to the rupee coming unstuck from the 35.85/86 level.

The state bank hit the market with its buy orders in the morning, dragging the rupee to 35.8750 soon after opening. It returned to the market several times during the day, buying at 35.8950 moments before the market closed.
"There were stray deals even at 35.9025 level," said a dealer at a leading Bombay bank.
Some dealers said the rupee may not see the 35.85 level for many days to come, but others said they were not sure whether THursday's month-end spurt in dollar demand would be sustained.
The forward dollar premia saw two-way movement. February and March delivery dollars in particular saw lot of action.
The six-month annualised premium ended the day at 7.36 percent compared to the previous close of 7.20 percent, reflecting the paying pressure from banks seeking forward cover, dealers said.
